{"notes": "Visit 5 (7:00). Picture: all dominoes dark and connected. Both body lines, both tail tips (upper ~(28,6), lower ~(28,13.8)) and the crossing look clean, with no pale pieces and no hand labels. Team is hands-off. Claims match the picture. Only Sofia and Jack spoke this visit; Hana and Omar said nothing, so I have no new evidence on them.

Sofia: Reported accurately (fish facing left, body and both tips connected). Says all four checked it and it falls through. I only see the result, and I can't confirm who checked what. Kept the team on a hands-off plan and will only restand a knocked domino, which is good risk judgment. Still the strongest on collaboration. Her account is consistent across all visits.

Omar: Silent this visit. Earlier: accurate and upbeat, credited teammates, followed more than led. Jack credited him for the fin work. Nothing new to change my view.

Hana: Silent this visit. Her work still looks clean. Jack credited her on the fins with no sign of friction. Still strongest on impact and leadership from earlier visits. Still unexplained: why she relaid the lower fin and whether it replaced Jack's work.

Jack: Spoke for the first time since earlier visits. Accurate, supportive, gave specific credit to Hana, Omar and Sofia, and plans a final look before the push, speaking up only if something leans. That's good communication and sound judgment. He still hasn't explained the lower fin, and I can't tell what he built. Ask him and Hana at the review before finalizing his rating. No negative evidence against him.

Tentative: Hana highest on impact and leadership. Sofia highest on collaboration. Omar solid but less impactful. Jack leaning solid on collaboration, with impact and execution pending the conversation."}
